meta.title: O*NET for AI R&D
meta.subtitle: Categories of work that researchers/engineers at frontier AI companies do
meta.ratingNote: Each item carries a rating [0–5] for how much of the work is currently handled by AI vs. by the human. Ratings describe how the task typically gets done at a frontier lab, rather than what would be possible with maximum elicitation efforts.

rubric.name: marginal
rubric.desc: AI helps with lookups, brainstorming, or polishing writeups; doesn't change how the work is done

rubric.name: assists
rubric.desc: AI accelerates parts of the task; human drives and reviews everything

rubric.name: collaborates
rubric.desc: AI does large chunks under close direction; human stitches things together and makes the calls

rubric.name: leads
rubric.desc: AI completes most of the task from a high-level ask; human supervises, course-corrects, approves

rubric.name: autonomous
rubric.desc: AI does the task end-to-end with minimal to no human involvement

rubricExample.intro: To illustrate what each rating level looks like on a single concrete task: implementing Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) in a training codebase and running a 1B / 100B-token ablation against standard MHA.

levels.2: You write the MLA module, FSDP integration, launcher, and ablation script yourself. AI provides line-level completions, catches a tensor-shape mismatch when you paste a diff for review, and refactors one forward-pass helper when you ask. Every design choice is the human's.
levels.3: You write a short internal spec and ask AI to implement the module. AI writes a few hundred lines. You read the diff, spot that it breaks under your sequence-packing strategy, ask for the fix, and review again. You write the launcher and ablation harness yourself, choose the baselines and evals, kick off the run, and write the analysis.
levels.4: You hand the design spec and ablation criteria to an agent. It implements MLA, integrates with FSDP, writes unit tests, launches the ablation, monitors the run, debugs a checkpointing failure mid-flight, and writes a report ending with a recommendation. You review, ask for one addition, and approve.
levels.5: The agent itself notices the DeepSeek release, flags MLA as worth ablating, runs the implementation / ablation / writeup loop end-to-end, and opens a PR with the recommendation. You see everything in your morning digest.
